config.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Family video call planning a cousin's wedding

personas.name: Agnieszka
personas.goals: A schedule that runs to the minute
personas.hidden_agenda: Feels her sister leaves everything to her

personas.name: Patrick
personas.goals: Pay his share and not a cent more
personas.hidden_agenda: Quietly worried about money after a rough year

personas.name: Zofia
personas.goals: Get through planning without a family fight

personas.name: Danny
personas.goals: Help, and be funny while doing it
personas.hidden_agenda: Lost the groomsmen's suit fitting receipt

pack.title: Zofia and Marcus's wedding - family call

agenda.title: Guests and seating
agenda.goal: Lock the headcount and start the seating plan

agenda.title: Money
agenda.goal: Be clear about who is paying for what

agenda.title: Rehearsal and the morning
agenda.goal: Agree the rehearsal and the wedding-morning schedule

agenda.title: Registry and gifts
agenda.goal: Check the registry and the honeymoon fund

facts.statement: Rehearsal starts at 5:00 pm on Friday
Hair and makeup start at 8:30 am

beats.summary: The headcount; Danny inflates it and nobody checks; seating starts; a fantasy football tangent
Who pays what; Patrick overstates his contribution and the room goes quiet
The rehearsal and the morning; Agnieszka gets the rehearsal time wrong and fixes it later
The registry and the honeymoon fund

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Okay, everyone is here. Zofia, the guest list first, because the venue wants numbers.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Okay so, we're at a hundred and thirty-six confirmed.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: That's more than we said.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Marcus's mom keeps adding people. Every week there's a new second cousin.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Maybe we cap it somewhere and tell her, politely.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: A hundred and fifty, give or take. It's going to be a party.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: And how many tables does that mean?

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Fourteen tables, ten at each, and a few spare seats.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: Fourteen tables. When I got married there were six.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: When you got married, Uncle Pat, there were also no phones.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: The seating plan. Where do the Brennan grandparents go?

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Near the front, but not near the speakers. Grandpa's hearing aid squeals.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Also, my fantasy league is a disaster. I'm last.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: I don't know what that is.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: It's like gambling, but with spreadsheets and no money.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Danny. Seating.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: I'll do a first draft of the seating chart this weekend and share it.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Put Marcus's mother where she can see everything. It'll keep her calm.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: That's actually smart.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Money. I know nobody wants to, but we have to.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: Your mother and I put in fifteen thousand. That's our part.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Dad. It was ten. We talked about it at Easter.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: Ten. Yes. Ten. I'm sorry, I was thinking of what we'd hoped.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Awkward.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: The total budget is twenty-four thousand. So the rest is Zofia and Marcus, and his parents.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: And we already paid the three thousand deposit for the venue.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: What's the bar going to cost?

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Thirty-two a head for the package.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: Thirty-two times a hundred and thirty-six. That's a lot of beer.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: It's not just beer, it's also wine.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Could we do a cash bar after ten o'clock? Lots of weddings do.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: I'd rather that than a bill nobody can pay.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Okay so, open bar until ten, then cash bar. That's fine.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Who's paying for the rehearsal dinner, by the way?

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Patrick, are you okay? You've gone quiet.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: I'm fine. It's been a long year, that's all.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: The schedule. The rehearsal on Friday is at six.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Six works for me. I finish work at five.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: And the morning? What time do we start?

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Hair and makeup at eight thirty, at the hotel.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Eight thirty is so early. Maybe we push it to nine?

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Eight thirty is late. The photographer comes at one, and you need to be dressed by then.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Is the photographer the guy with the drone?

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: No drone. I said no drone.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: What do the groomsmen do in the morning? Anything?

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: You collect the suits by nine and you're at the church by one thirty. Sober.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: About the suits. I may have lost the fitting receipt.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Danny!

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: I know the shop! They know me! It's fine. I'll go in Thursday and sort it out with them.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: My cat has a vet appointment that Thursday, actually. Surgery on her paw.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Oh no, poor Pierogi. Is she okay?

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: She'll be fine. She's tougher than me.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: I'm looking at the booking email. The rehearsal is at five, not six. Sorry, I had the dinner time in my head.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Five. Then I'll leave work early.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Rehearsal at five, dinner at six thirty, and nobody is late.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: The registry. There are like forty things still left on it.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: I checked last night, it's twenty-three. People bought a lot this week.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Oh, nice. Twenty-three.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: Has anyone heard whether Aunt Halina is actually coming?

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: And the honeymoon fund? How's that going?

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Eighteen fifty so far. Enough for the flights, almost.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: Is my picture frozen? I see myself upside down.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: You're fine, Uncle Pat. You're just upside down.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Someone should remind the Polish side about the registry. They don't use the internet much.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: I'll call my brother on Sunday and tell him. He'll tell everyone else.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: Thank you, Dad.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Does anyone know if the date is on the invitations right? I keep getting asked if it's the sixth or the seventh.

turns.speaker: Zofia
turns.text: It's the sixth. September sixth. It's on the invitations.

turns.speaker: Agnieszka
turns.text: Then we're done. Next call in two weeks. Same time.

turns.speaker: Danny
turns.text: Same bat time, same bat channel.

turns.speaker: Patrick
turns.text: I don't know what that means either.
